subject.title: Orphaned lock files not cleared on gateway restart when PID matches current process

question: What recovery contract should OpenClaw use when a session `.jsonl.lock` is owned by the live gateway PID but no longer corresponds to a safe active transcript writer?
rationale: Force-reclaim, timeout-and-watchdog, lock poisoning, and preserve-live-holder behavior have different session-state and transcript-concurrency tradeoffs that automation cannot safely choose from source inspection alone.

options.title: Choose one recovery contract
options.body: Adopt a single owner-approved policy that covers startup cleanup, restart recovery, retained-lock teardown, and maxHold reclaim, then require focused tests and live proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Split remaining live-holder cases
options.body: Close only the original boot-cleanup slice as shipped and keep narrower issues such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87483 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/100872 as the active policy threads.

options.title: Wait for live current-main fixture
options.body: Defer policy changes until a packaged gateway fixture reproduces the same-PID recovery failure on current main, accepting continued manual cleanup reports in the meantime.

recommendation.title: Choose one recovery contract
recommendation.body: Adopt a single owner-approved policy that covers startup cleanup, restart recovery, retained-lock teardown, and maxHold reclaim, then require focused tests and live proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest current session-lock policy history and is explicitly pulled into related live-holder PR review discussion.
